title: Does Kin Selection Explain Altruism?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore kin selection, the evolutionary theory that organisms can pass on genes indirectly by helping relatives reproduce, as a answer to the puzzle of biological altruism. They cover Darwin's natural selection and survival of the fittest, the problem of sterile worker bees and other altruistic behavior, William Hamilton's inclusive fitness and Hamilton's rule, Florida scrub jay helping studies, meerkat sentinels, group selection as a rival explanation, the E. O. Wilson versus Richard Dawkins dispute, and the freeloader effect. The episode ends with a listener mail about life in Sweden.

segments.title: Opening banter and trivia
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Jerry, the show's mysterious producer, and recall a trivia question about Charles Darwin marrying his first cousin. They tease Jennifer Connelly's role in a Darwin film and introduce the episode's evolution theme.

segments.title: Natural selection and the reproduction puzzle
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck explain Darwin's natural selection, survival of the fittest, and reproductive fitness, using variation as a key driver. They note that gene passing is the point of reproduction and that many organisms behave in ways that don't pass on their own genes, which poses a problem for the theory.

segments.title: Altruistic behavior in bees and the kin selection explanation
segments.summary: They describe sterile or non-reproducing worker bees who serve the queen and raise young, which contradicts individual gene passing. Hamilton, a graduate student in the 1960s, proposed inclusive fitness and kin selection. A study of Florida scrub jays found most helpers assisted parents or siblings.

segments.title: Hamilton's rule and the math of altruism
segments.summary: The hosts walk through Hamilton's rule, in which the benefit to the receiver multiplied by relatedness must exceed the cost to the altruist, with the rule summarized as rB minus C greater than zero. They discuss that the benefit generally needs to be about double for altruism to persist.

segments.title: Meerkat sentinels and social animal examples
segments.summary: They discuss ants, wasps and insect workers, meerkat sentinels who warn the group, and meerkat cooperative care of pups. They also make a loose analogy to a traffic intersection and human behavior.

segments.title: Group selection, E. O. Wilson and Richard Dawkins
segments.summary: Group selection is introduced as an alternative in which altruism benefits the whole group rather than relatives. E. O. Wilson, a sociobiologist, reversed his support of kin selection in favor of group selection, drawing criticism from Richard Dawkins, who also described the freeloader effect from The Selfish Gene.

segments.title: Closing discussion and search pointer
segments.summary: Chuck raises the question of whether helping reduces net offspring, and they suggest searching the HowStuffWorks site for kin selection.

segments.title: Listener mail: Sweden rules
segments.summary: A listener from Sweden describes taxes, free healthcare, free university with a stipend, long parental leave, and free kindergarten, along with problems such as privatization and rising xenophobia.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and point to social media and the website for more information.
